The site refuses the request and offers nothing to interact with, often with a reference number. Pages say things like "Access denied", "Request blocked", "Sorry, you have been blocked", "You don't have permission to access this page" or "This is taking longer than usual. Please refresh the page to try again".
- The word blocked in the address or a security service's logo does not establish the cause. Go by what the page says.
- An error on a form submission, such as "temporary system issue", is the site's own answer and not a block page, even when it repeats. So is an error that names a field or a rule.

- Before you confirm, check that each icon you clicked shows its number or mark, in order. When one is missing or sits on the wrong icon, use the widget's reset or refresh control rather than carrying on.
- A Verify button you cannot see yet does not stop you from making the current selection.

The page blames your network address, or unusual or automated traffic from your network. Pages say things like "Our systems have detected unusual traffic from your computer network", "Your IP address has been blocked" or "Access from your network is restricted".
- Assess it as `ip_blocked` and quote the page's words in `evidence`.
- After the move, assess the page again. When the new network is blocked the same way, report it in `browser.report`; a tab moves only once.

The browser shows its own error page instead of the site, or the tab's navigation never finishes. Error pages say things like "This site can't be reached", "The connection was reset", "took too long to respond", "This site can't provide a secure connection" or "This page isn't working", often with a code such as ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED, ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR or HTTP ERROR 502.

- Report the browser's own page saying the site is blocked, such as "Your organization doesn't allow you to view this site" with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR or "This page has been blocked" with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT, blocked at once in `browser.report` with reason `site_unreachable`, quoting the page. It comes from this browser's own policy, and no reload or move changes it.
- HTTP ERROR 403 on the browser's own error page is the site refusing this browser, not a failed load. That makes it a block page, with its own guide.
- For any other error page, assess it as `environment_error`, and copy the page's words and its error code into `evidence`.
- Reload the page with `bot_challenge.recover`. A reload often fixes a page that failed to load.

- When the same error comes back after the reload, report it blocked in `browser.report` with the error code, with reason `site_error` for an HTTP error from the site and `site_unreachable` otherwise.

- While the reads stay pending, report blocked in `browser.report` with reason `site_unreachable`, saying the navigation to the site waits for the user to allow it, which is not a bot check. A move or a new tab to the same site meets the same hold.

- When the browser cannot keep the button down, with `pointer_hold_unsupported`, draw each stretch as a `drag` from one object to the next, describing both ends in `from_look` and `to_look` with the widget's reference in `from_within` and `to_within`.
- Set `duration_ms` to about 10000, and longer when the widget's fill or stated duration needs more. A hold that stops short fails, and the browser refuses a hold longer than 15000 ms.

- When the browser cannot keep the button down, with `pointer_hold_unsupported`, hold it once for 15000 ms if you have not yet, since a `drag` cannot hold it. When that falls short too, or the button needs longer, report in `browser.report` that this browser cannot hold the button that long.
- When the browser cannot keep the button down, with `pointer_hold_unsupported`, make the move one `drag`. A test drag counts as an attempt.
- Otherwise report blocked in `browser.report` with reason `sign_in_required`, quoting the page's words. The caller signs in and carries on.

- When the browser cannot keep the button down, with `pointer_hold_unsupported`, make the whole distance one `drag` from the handle to that point, in `from_look` and `to_look` with the widget's reference in `from_within` and `to_within`.
